told_more: The record gave dates and causes for every event (cannery owner's widow lets the shop, bakery, heirs who cannot agree to sell, a break-in), the life before 1989 (A built 1912, B burned and rebuilt 1936, C's 1971 windows, D empty from 1986), and things a view cannot show at all (repaints, a leaking roof, a house empty but not boarded). The views only showed form, and they led me to wrong dates and a wrong link between D and E. The views were still reliable on what visibly changed: B's shop and balcony, D's boards coming off, E's boards going on, A's shopfront going, C's windows. I missed one, C's 1998 upper windows, until I looked again.

misled.claim: E was lived in in 1989 and 2000 because its windows were open and glazed, and I called its care 'kept' in 2000 (the record: the last owner died in 1993 and it stood empty and neglected from then, boarded only in 2008)
A traded as a shop through 2010 (the record: the cafe closed in 2009, so the shop was empty in 2010, though the shopfront was still there)
A's shop closed between 2010 and 2020 and the shopfront came out then (the record: the shop closed in 2009, and only the shopfront was taken out in 2016)
E's occupant may have moved down to D, so D reopened as E closed (the record: D was bought by a young family in 2007, E had stood empty since 1993 and was boarded after a break-in in 2008; no link)

C's roof and walls were untouched across the whole period and nothing changed on it between 1989 and 2000 (the record: the upper-floor windows were restored with copies in 1998; I missed this, though on a second look the gable window does change between the 1989 and 2000 frames)

C's upper windows and ground-floor windows were original in 1989 to 2010, and C was kept in its original form before 1989 (the record: all of C's windows were replaced cheaply in 1971, the upper ones were copied back in 1998)

C's ground-floor windows gained casings and sills between 2010 and 2020 as a renewal (the record: factory 'old style' windows fitted in 2011 in the wall facing down the lane, so look-alikes, not a restoration)
E's upper and ground-floor windows were original in 1989 and 2000 (the record: front windows replaced in 1965)
D's windows were original again in 2010 and 2020 after the boards came off (the record: restored in 2007 with copies of the old gable windows, front windows replaced in 1965)
D's roof was original and not neglected in 1989 and 2000 (the record: by 1995 the roof let in water; nothing of this shows in the views)
A was 'kept' in 1989 (the record: not repainted from 1949 to 1996 and the shop empty 1974 to 1988; paint age is invisible in the grey views)
B's extension is a glazed veranda with a balcony above (the record holds only a balcony over the lane, 2003; the glazed part below is not in it)
A dark box or hatch on B's front above the awning appeared between 1989 and 2000 (the record has no such event; the bakery's sign is the only thing nearby)
A's upper-floor bay window is original (the record does not mention a bay)
D's lean-to is on its side (the record: at the back, a shed added in 1950)
The corner grew busier between 2000 and 2010 (the record: the cafe in A closed in 2009 because the quay road's trade had gone up the hill, though B's balcony and D's family point the other way)
My Part 1 year guesses of 1905 to 1950, read from the shopfronts, mansard roof and veranda (the real frames are 1989 to 2020; the views carried no era cue)

views_showed: At a glance, who is gone and who has come back: D's boards at eye level and from the steps, and E's boards closing the view up the lane, so the lane reads as having swapped its empty end from D to E, even though the record holds them as two unrelated stories.

That A's shopfront was an insertion: it cut across the window rhythm of the upper floor, and when it came out the three ground-floor windows lined up again with the upper ones, so the 'copies of the windows it had covered' are visible as a restored order.
How little changed around the corner: the neighbouring houses stay identical in all four years, so only these five carry the history, and the city view shows B's and A's front changes from above.

That B's shopfront reads as a blank, unglazed panel under a fascia, which a page that says 'bakery' does not show, and that B changed most, twice in 13 years, while the rest of the corner hardly moved.
The geometry the record only states in words: D on its rock above the landing and E at the head of the stairs, so a boarded house is what the visitor sees at the top of the steps.
